To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) DG methods are surprisingly good at alleviating the dataset-bias problem, and that 2) the dataset bias is not the most challenging problem in DG, and that 3) DG methods need to be developed to handle the bigger challenge of domain generalization.

(1) existing DG methods perform surprisingly well on photo-only DG benchmarks, which are not sufficiently challenging; (2) a simple CNN baseline performs surprisingly well on the new DG benchmark we propose, which is both more practically-relevant, and harder; and (3) our proposed low-rank DG method outperforms the existing methods on the new benchmark.
